USS Constellation

CVA-64, “Connie”; Kitty Hawk class; commissioned 27 October 1961; at Yankee Station from the first day of the air war to the last

Station. Yankee Station, Gulf of Tonkin; seven combat deployments 1964–1973

US figures are the Defense Casualty Analysis System by year of death; the last column is the range in project 55. Every Vietnam page carries this box.

The ship, one line item each

1964-08-05Pierce Arrow: with Ticonderoga, launches the first retaliatory strikes after the Tonkin Gulf incident, against the torpedo-boat bases and the Vinh oil depot. Lt. (j.g.) Richard Sather, an A-1 pilot from Connie, is the first Navy pilot killed in the war; Lt. (j.g.) Everett Alvarez, an A-4 pilot from Connie, is shot down and becomes the first Navy prisoner. He is held eight years and six months.
1966–1967Second and third deployments: Rolling Thunder over the delta; the air wing loses aircraft to the guns that page 6 of the workbook describes.
1968–1969Fourth deployment: the bombing halt of 31 October 1968 comes with Connie on station; the wing turns to the Trail.
1971-11 to 1972-07Sixth deployment. 10 May 1972: the first day of Linebacker I, Connie's fighters shoot down seven MiGs; Lt. Randy Cunningham and Lt. (j.g.) Willie Driscoll of VF-96 take three in one sortie and become the Navy's first aces of the war, then are hit by a SAM on the way out and ejected over the gulf, picked up by a Marine helicopter.
1972-11The sit-down: about 130 Black sailors refuse to reboard at San Diego after racial incidents aboard; the Navy calls it a work stoppage rather than a mutiny, and the Z-grams follow.
1973-01 to 1973-10Seventh deployment: on station when the Accords are signed; her last combat sorties are over Laos and Cambodia.
1975-04Not at the fall — at Bremerton for overhaul. Enterprise, Coral Sea, Midway and Hancock take the helicopters.
2003-08-07Decommissioned after Iraq; scrapped at Brownsville, 2015–2017.

Numbers

Air wingabout 70–80 aircraft; CVW-14 for most of the war, CVW-9 in 1971–72
Sorties in a line periodroughly 100–130 a day at full tempo, in cycles of about ninety minutes
Combat deployments7, 1964–1973; about 30 months on the line in all
Crewabout 5,000, of whom perhaps a tenth ever saw the coast

The game

You are Connie. Each tap launches a sortie; each aircraft you spot on deck launches on its own, on the ninety-minute cycle, forever. The game does not count losses, which is the one thing the ship counted.

Launch — resource: sorties; unit: aircraft.
